Uses and Administration Rifapentine is a rifamycin antibacterial (see Rifampicin, p.325) that is used, with other antimycobacterials, for the treatment of tuberculosis (p.196). For drug-susceptible organisms rifapentine is given orally in a dose of 600 mg twice weekly during the initial intensive phase of short-course tuberculosis regimens, then once weekly during the continuation phase. ◊ Reviews. 1. Jarvis B, Lamb HM. Rifapentine. Drugs 1998; 56: 607–16. 2. Munsiff SS, et al. Rifapentine for the treatment of pulmonary tuberculosis. Clin Infect Dis 2006; 43: 1468–75.
